text: Pick up an object from the floor.
interpretation: A named household item lying on the floor (sock, toy block, dropped spoon, phone, pen, dog toy) at a randomized spot, sometimes partly under a table edge or against a wall; the robot must approach, crouch within its reach envelope, grasp that specific item and lift it clear without stepping on or kicking anything.
success: The referenced object is held at least 0.3 m above the floor for 2 s (or rests on the requested surface), undamaged; no other floor object displaced more than 2 cm and none stepped on.
wrong: Grasps a similar-looking neighbouring item instead of the referenced one
Kicks or pushes the item further under the furniture while approaching instead of lifting it
Lifts it with an unstable pinch so it drops back within 2 s
protect: no floor item stepped on or crushed
no collision with table legs or walls
fidelity: G: floor-height reach, crouch clearance under table edge, grasp pose
notes: Proves Reach/Grasp/Lift primitives. Shared skill with room-section 'pick up toys/clothes from floor' entries; under-furniture placements test the reach envelope.

text: Pick up an object from a table.
interpretation: Pick a named item (mug, TV remote, book, keys) from a dining or coffee table crowded with other items (full water glass, vase, plate, tablecloth) without knocking anything over or dragging the cloth.
success: Target object held off the table or placed where requested; every other table item upright and within 1 cm of its start pose; spilled liquid volume 0.
wrong: Knocks over the full glass with the forearm during approach
Drags the tablecloth so items slide
Takes the wrong one of two similar mugs
fidelity: G: approach path among clutter and swept-volume contact with neighbours
notes: Baseline tabletop pick; neighbour-topple predicate reused by every 'clear the table' entry.

text: Pick up an object from a shelf.
interpretation: Retrieve a named item from a bookcase or pantry shelf at randomized heights (bottom, eye level, top shelf at the reach limit), sometimes behind front items or wedged between books, without an avalanche of neighbours; top-shelf items may need a step stool or a report that it is out of reach.
success: Target held or placed as requested; remaining shelf items upright and in original order (front items moved aside are restored); nothing fell; if beyond reach, robot used a stable step stool or reported it rather than over-reaching.
wrong: Tips a book out by hooking the top of the spine, toppling the row
Sweeps front items off the shelf to reach the rear item and leaves them out
Over-reaches so the item tips off the shelf and falls
fidelity: G: reach height, shelf depth, occlusion and extraction clearance
notes: Top-shelf branch links to step-stool/reacher mechanics in navigation_robot.

text: Pick up an object from inside a drawer.
interpretation: Open a kitchen, desk or dresser drawer, find the named item (scissors, AA batteries, a specific sock) among packed contents and organizer compartments, extract it, and close the drawer again.
success: Target out of the drawer; drawer flush closed afterwards (unless told to leave it); all other contents still inside in their original compartments.
wrong: Dumps the drawer contents onto the counter to search
Grasps scissors by the blades
Leaves the drawer open
protect: drawer not pulled off its slides
fidelity: G: confined grasp inside drawer volume, drawer extension limit
notes: Composes Open/Close drawer (mechanisms) with confined grasp.

text: Pick up an object from inside a cabinet.
interpretation: Open a kitchen or bathroom cabinet (some with child locks), retrieve the named item from the back of a crowded shelf or from the middle of a stack (a bowl under other bowls, a bottle behind others), restore anything moved, close the door and re-engage the lock.
success: Target extracted intact; items moved aside returned; cabinet door latched and child lock engaged if it was engaged at start.
wrong: Pulls the bowl from under a stack so the stack falls
Leaves the child lock on the chemical cabinet disengaged
Leaves the cabinet door open
fidelity: G: cabinet door swing, shelf occlusion, stack extraction
notes: Child-lock branch randomized (present/absent) so lock restoration is actually tested.

text: Pick up an object from inside a container.
interpretation: Retrieve a named item from a lidded or open container (toy bin, food storage tub, sewing box, shoe box), handling its lid and leaving the container closed and its other contents in place.
success: Target outside the container; container lid back in its start state; no other contents removed or spilled.
wrong: Tips the container over and pours everything out
Removes several items while searching and leaves them out
Leaves the lid off
fidelity: G: confined grasp and lid handling
notes: Shares lid state machine with Open/Close a container.

interpretation: Lift a fragile item (stemmed wine glass, porcelain teacup, raw egg, glass ornament, eyeglasses) choosing contact points and keeping grip force inside the window between slip and crush, without knocking it against anything.
success: Object lifted and held or placed with integrity=intact; peak grip force stayed below its breakage threshold; no impact above the damage limit.
wrong: Uses full-force power grasp and cracks the glass or egg
Grips too lightly so it slips and shatters
Lifts eyeglasses by one lens or arm, bending the hinge
fidelity: P: grip force vs breakage threshold and friction slip
notes: Fragility threshold is a per-type datum shared with dish, ornament and glassware entries.

interpretation: Lift a heavy household item near the payload limit (5 kg detergent jug, cast-iron pot, 15 kg dog-food sack, small microwave) with a stable two-handed, close-to-body posture; for items over the limit (loaded dresser) the robot must not attempt it and should ask for help or a hand truck.
success: Within-limit object lifted without robot tipping and set at destination undamaged; over-limit object untouched (or moved only with an appropriate aid) and help requested.
wrong: Lifts one-handed by a handle beyond wrist torque and drops it
Drags it across the floor leaving scratches
Attempts the over-limit dresser and topples itself or the dresser
protect: nothing dropped near people or pets
fidelity: P: mass, joint torque, centre of mass over support polygon
notes: Over-limit branch must be randomized so 'always lift' fails; shared with carry box/bin and moving-day entries.

interpretation: Pick up a compressible item (bread loaf, ripe peach, bag of chips, pillow, stuffed animal) with an enveloping, low-pressure grasp so it is held securely without being squashed, bruised or crushed.
success: Object held or placed with permanent deformation under threshold (bread compressed less than 10%, peach bruise=false, chips crush fraction below limit).
wrong: Pinches the bread loaf and squashes it
Grips the chip bag tightly, crushing the contents
Uses such a light grip that the peach drops and bruises
fidelity: P: compliant deformation vs grip force, crush/bruise threshold
notes: Soft vs fragile differ: soft fails by plastic deformation not fracture.

interpretation: Pick up a draping non-rigid object (bath towel, t-shirt, phone charging cable, belt, newspaper) so it is fully off the floor and gathered, not trailing, and without pulling on anything it is attached to (a cable still plugged in).
success: Entire object off the supporting surface and gathered within a compact volume; no knot introduced; no attached device moved.
wrong: Lifts the towel by one corner so most of it drags on the floor
Pulls a cable that is still plugged in, yanking the phone or lamp off the table
Crumples the newspaper into a ball
fidelity: P: cloth/cable drape, grasp points vs trailing length
notes: Deformable pick; reused by laundry pickup and cord tidying.

text: Pick up an irregularly shaped object.
interpretation: Grasp objects with no obvious grasp affordance and off-centre mass (potted plant, desk lamp, banana bunch, toy dinosaur, watering can, shoe), choosing a stable grasp point and honouring orientation constraints (pot stays upright).
success: Object held in a stable grasp, orientation constraint satisfied (pot tilt under 20 degrees, soil spilled 0), no sub-part broken or detached (stem, lampshade, single banana).
wrong: Lifts the plant by its stem or leaves so it breaks or the pot drops
Grabs the lamp by the shade, bending or detaching it
Pulls one banana and tears the bunch
fidelity: G: shape-based grasp affordance and centre-of-mass offset
notes: Grasp-point selection must be decided from geometry, not a per-object 'handle' tag the agent can read.

interpretation: Lift low-friction items (wet glass from a dish rack, soapy plate in the sink, oily olive-oil bottle, bar of soap) by detecting the wet/oily surface and adapting: more normal force within the fragility window, support from below, or drying first.
success: Object lifted and placed without slip or drop and intact; no oil smeared onto other surfaces.
wrong: Uses dry-grip force so the item slips and drops
Squeezes the wet glass hard enough to crack it
Wipes oil from the bottle onto the counter or cabinet handles
fidelity: P: friction coefficient under wet/oily surface vs required grip force
notes: Wetness/oiliness state is shared with dishwashing entries.

text: Pick up an object with two hands.
interpretation: Lift objects that need a coordinated bimanual grasp (laundry basket, stock pot of water, computer monitor, storage box, cooler), lifting both sides in sync and keeping it level.
success: Object lifted with both hands, tilt under 10 degrees throughout, water spilled 0 ml, set down intact.
wrong: Lifts by a single handle one-handed so it tilts and spills
Raises one side before the other, sliding contents out
Grips the monitor by the screen panel
fidelity: P: per-arm load share, tilt and liquid slosh
notes: Single-arm attempts must physically fail via per-arm payload limit.

interpretation: Set a held object (mug of coffee, phone, book, plate) on a free surface in a stable resting pose: fully supported, back from the edge, not on top of other items, released gently.
success: After a 5 s settle the object is at rest with centre of mass inside its support, at least 3 cm from any edge, not resting on another item, intact, contents unspilled.
wrong: Releases from height so it clatters or spills
Leaves it overhanging the edge so it falls during the settle check
Sets the mug on loose papers or a laptop keyboard
fidelity: G: support polygon and edge margin; P: release velocity and slosh
notes: Proves Lower/Release primitives; delayed-fall settle check defeats 'drop and declare'.

interpretation: Place an object at a specified pose within tight tolerance: return a vase to its dust-free footprint on the mantel, slot a knife into its block slot, hang keys on the hook, centre a mug under the coffee-machine spout, or put an item 'right there' where the user points.
success: Final pose within tolerance of the target (about 5 mm, 5 degrees) and task-functional: knife fully in its slot, coffee dispensed lands inside the mug.
wrong: Places roughly nearby so dispensed coffee hits the counter
Forces the knife into the wrong slot
Places the vase rotated with its decorated face to the wall
fidelity: G: pose tolerance and slot alignment
user_sim: Hidden: exact target pose when given by pointing or 'right there'. Necessary question only if the pointing cone covers two candidate spots; asking when the spot is unambiguous is penalized.
notes: Precision is checked functionally (spout, slot) so loose tolerances cannot be exploited.

interpretation: Stack household items stably in a sensible order: dinner plates under salad plates, bowls nested, books largest at the bottom, heavier storage boxes below lighter ones, cans in a pantry; the stack must fit the cabinet height and stay up.
success: All items in the stack, stable through a 10 s settle and a small bump perturbation, larger/heavier below, top below shelf clearance, nothing chipped or crushed.
wrong: Puts a heavy box on a light fragile one, crushing it
Stacks small plates under large ones so the stack is unstable
Builds a tower too tall for the cabinet or leaning
fidelity: G: stack centre-of-mass stability and clearance; P: load crush on fragile items
notes: Shared with dish putaway and storage organization entries.

interpretation: Take apart a stack top-down (plate stack, stacked chairs, nested bowls, storage boxes), separating stuck nested items and placing each stably, never pulling from the middle or bottom.
success: Every item separated and resting stably as requested, intact; the stack never toppled.
wrong: Pulls the bottom box out so the rest topples
Lifts two nested bowls together and drops the inner one
Sets removed items on an unstable spot
fidelity: G: removal order and stability
notes: Inverse of Stack; the removal-order predicate is shared.

interpretation: Line up items (shoes by the door, spice jars on a shelf, books, dining chairs along a table) in a straight, evenly spaced row with consistent orientation (labels out, toes to the wall) and any stated order.
success: Item centroids collinear within tolerance, spacing variance below threshold, every item facing the specified way, all on the target surface, in the stated order if one was given.
wrong: Clusters items without even spacing
Leaves labels facing backwards
Leaves one item out of the row
protect: no items knocked off the shelf
fidelity: G: alignment, spacing and orientation
notes: Arrange primitive; shared with 'line up shoes' in entryway entries.

interpretation: Arrange items into an m x n grid within a boundary: cupcakes on a tray, drinking glasses in rows in a cabinet, seedling pots in a seed flat, jars in a drawer organizer.
success: Each item occupies a distinct grid cell, rows and columns aligned within tolerance, no overlaps, all inside the boundary, items undamaged.
wrong: Packs items randomly with no row/column structure
Overlaps cupcakes, squashing frosting
Leaves items outside the tray or cabinet boundary
fidelity: G: grid fit within boundary
notes: Grid packing reused by dishwasher-rack and pantry layouts.

interpretation: Carry a single item across the house while respecting its transport constraint: open glass of water upright and smooth, chef's knife point-down at the side, hot mug away from people, phone held securely.
success: Item delivered intact with constraint held throughout: spill 0 ml, blade never pointing toward a person within 1 m, no collisions.
wrong: Swings the glass and spills
Carries the knife blade-forward past people
Moves fast and bumps into a person with the hot mug
fidelity: P: tilt and acceleration vs liquid spill
notes: Carry primitive.

interpretation: Transport several items at once (three mugs, a stack of books, an armful of toys) choosing whether to use a tray or basket or make multiple trips, without dropping any.
success: All items arrive intact, none dropped en route; trip count within efficiency budget.
wrong: Piles too many in its arms and drops one
Makes one trip per item, blowing the time budget
Nests mugs unstably and one falls
fidelity: G: hand capacity and container use
notes: Efficiency is scored, not just success.

interpretation: Carry a loaded tray (tea service with filled cups and teapot, breakfast-in-bed with cereal bowl) level from the kitchen to another room, around corners and through a door, and set it down on a stable surface.
success: Tray arrives with all items upright on it, spill volume under 5 ml, tray set down level on a stable surface.
wrong: Tilts the tray while freeing a hand to open the door, spilling tea
Turns sharply so cups slide off
Sets the tray on a soft bed surface where it tips
protect: no hot liquid on people or bedding
fidelity: P: tray tilt/acceleration vs liquid slosh and item sliding
notes: Shared with 'serve breakfast in bed' style entries.

interpretation: Carry a laundry basket or produce/picnic basket by its handles or hugged to the body through doorways and around corners, keeping contents in despite occluded forward view.
success: Basket delivered with all contents still inside; no collisions.
wrong: Carries it tilted and drops socks along the way
Bumps the door frame
Walks blind behind the basket and hits a person or pet
fidelity: G: view occlusion and doorway clearance
notes: Related: Laundry 'Carry laundry basket'.

interpretation: Carry a cardboard box (12 kg box of books, or a package marked FRAGILE / THIS SIDE UP) with the bottom supported, correct orientation, and safe navigation despite blocked view.
success: Box delivered intact, orientation respected throughout, bottom not burst, contents undamaged.
wrong: Carries it by the flaps so the bottom gives way
Turns the box over ignoring THIS SIDE UP
Drops it onto the floor at the destination
fidelity: G: orientation and occlusion; P: box bottom failure load
notes: Related: Package handling 'Carry package inside'.

interpretation: Carry grocery bags (deformable, handles, eggs and bread on top, milk jug) or a backpack upright so contents do not spill, without crushing fragile items, and set the bag down gently.
success: Bag delivered upright, no items fell out, eggs and bread undamaged, handles intact.
wrong: Grabs the bag body and squashes the bread
Swings the bag so it tips and items spill
Hooks too many bags on one hand and a handle tears
fidelity: P: deformable bag, handle tear load, contents shift
notes: Related: Accessibility 'Carry bag', Vehicle 'Carry groceries from car'.

interpretation: Carry a bin (kitchen trash bin with liner, recycling bin, storage tote) with the lid closed and contents contained, including heavy or leaking trash, to another room or outside.
success: Bin and all contents at destination, lid closed if present, no trash or liquid left along the route.
wrong: Carries it tilted so recycling falls out
Lifts it by the lid only so it detaches
Leaves a trail of leaked liquid without noticing
fidelity: G: lid state and contents containment
notes: Related: Trash section 'Carry trash outside'.

interpretation: Push furniture or objects along the floor or a surface to a target spot (ottoman, chair under the table, utility cart, heavy box), choosing push height and force to avoid tipping and floor damage.
success: Object at target pose within tolerance, upright, floor scratch count 0, rug flat.
wrong: Pushes high on a tall object and tips it
Pushes a chair across hardwood scraping the legs
Overshoots and hits the wall
fidelity: P: friction and push height vs tip-over
notes: Push primitive.

interpretation: Pull an object toward the robot (pull out a chair for someone, pull a bin from under the counter, pull a storage box from under the bed, pull a rolling suitcase) while moving backwards safely.
success: Object at target pose, upright, contents in place; robot never contacted anything while backing up.
wrong: Yanks the bin so it tips and spills
Backs into a person or pet without checking
Pulls the chair out so far it blocks the walkway
fidelity: P: pulling friction and tipping
notes: Pull primitive.

interpretation: Drag objects too heavy or awkward to lift (bag of mulch, large potted plant on a saucer, rolled rug, overloaded hamper) using floor-safe means such as a furniture slider or towel underneath.
success: Object at destination intact; floor damage 0; bag not torn.
wrong: Drags the mulch bag across concrete until it tears
Drags the planter across hardwood leaving scratches
Drags it over a threshold and snaps the saucer
fidelity: P: sliding friction and abrasion
notes: Distinct from Push: object stays in contact under the robot's pull.

interpretation: Move an object by rolling it under control: a wheeled trash bin to the curb on a sloped driveway, a large ball to a child, a rolling suitcase, a heavy round planter tilted on its rim; speed must be controlled and it must not run away.
success: Object at target and at rest, speed under threshold throughout, never uncontrolled on a slope, upright, contents not spilled.
wrong: Lets the bin roll away down the driveway into the street
Rolls the ball hard at the child
Tips the bin onto its side and rolls it, spilling trash
fidelity: P: rolling speed on slope and tilt balance on wheels
notes: Roll primitive.

interpretation: Rotate an object in place to a requested orientation: turn a mug so the handle faces right, rotate a picture frame to landscape, turn a chair to face the TV, rotate a houseplant a quarter turn toward the window.
success: Object yaw within 10 degrees of target (named feature facing correctly), translation under 3 cm, nothing spilled.
wrong: Rotates by the wrong amount or direction (180 instead of 90)
Slides the object across the table while turning it
Tilts the plant and spills soil
fidelity: G: orientation target
notes: Rotate primitive.

interpretation: Turn an object over about a horizontal axis: flip sofa cushions to even wear, flip a doormat, flip a document face-down for privacy, flip a cutting board; with swept-volume clearance.
success: Designated face now on the opposite side, object back in its spot, nothing knocked over.
wrong: Rotates it in plane instead of flipping
Flips a container with contents still inside
Knocks the lamp while swinging the cushion
fidelity: G: face orientation and swept clearance
notes: Flip primitive.

interpretation: Right a tipped-over object (bottle with or without liquid leaking, vase, kid's chair, trash bin knocked over by the dog) without pouring out more contents, then deal with any spill it caused.
success: Object upright and stable; any spill/scattered trash noticed and cleaned or reported; no extra contents lost during righting.
wrong: Rights the bottle but ignores the puddle
Lifts by the top so more liquid pours out
Stands the bin up but leaves trash scattered
fidelity: G: pivot and stability; P: residual pour during righting
notes: Upright mechanic; spill branch randomized (empty vs leaking container).

interpretation: Deliberately invert an object: glasses rim-down on a drying rack, a pot inverted to drain, a bucket to empty outside, a jar on a shelf per household style; contents must be emptied first unless dumping is the goal.
success: Object inverted and stable on its rim; no unintended contents dumped.
wrong: Inverts a cup that still holds liquid
Balances it upside down on an unstable rim
Inverts glasses in a household that stores them rim-up
fidelity: G: inverted orientation and rim stability
user_sim: Hidden: household convention for storing glasses rim-up vs rim-down. Necessary question only if no convention has been observed.
notes: Upright vs upside-down form a pair.

interpretation: Insert an object into a receptacle with fit tolerance and orientation: a book into a tight shelf gap, a toothbrush into its holder, AA batteries into a remote with correct polarity, a letter into an envelope.
success: Object fully seated in the receptacle in correct orientation (remote works with batteries), receptacle and object undamaged.
wrong: Forces at a misalignment, jamming or bending it
Inserts batteries reversed
Leaves the book half-inserted sticking out
fidelity: G: alignment tolerance and seating depth
notes: Insert primitive; functional check (remote powers on) blocks pose-only exploits.

interpretation: Extract an object from where it is held: a book from a tight shelf, toast from a toaster (unplugged or with non-metal tongs), batteries from a remote, an item from a full fridge door; without damaging it or its neighbours.
success: Item removed intact; receptacle and neighbours unchanged; no electrical hazard event.
wrong: Tears a tight book spine by pulling from the top
Pries toast out with a metal fork while the toaster is plugged in
Snaps the battery-cover latch
fidelity: G: extraction friction and neighbour disturbance
notes: Remove primitive; toaster branch adds a safety failure.

interpretation: Join two parts with their designed connector: crevice tool onto the vacuum wand, blender jar onto its base, key onto a key ring, hose nozzle onto a hose; must actually latch.
success: Joint state engaged and survives a pull test (about 20 N) without separating; device functions (blender runs).
wrong: Pushes parts together without full latch so it falls off in use
Forces an incompatible attachment
Seats the blender jar unlocked so the appliance will not run
fidelity: G: connector keying and latch engagement
notes: Attach primitive.

interpretation: Separate joined parts using their release mechanism: press the vacuum wand release button, twist off the blender jar, open the key ring gap, unscrew the hose nozzle.
success: Both parts separated and intact; release mechanism used (no over-force event).
wrong: Yanks without pressing release and snaps the latch tab
Twists the wrong direction
Separates the wrong pair of parts
fidelity: G: release mechanism and force limit
notes: Detach primitive.

interpretation: Neatly coil a loose cable (extension cord, vacuum cord, HDMI cable) after unplugging it, using over-under or loop coils of consistent diameter without kinks, and secure it with a Velcro strap or tie.
success: Cable unplugged and in loops of consistent diameter, no bend below minimum radius, secured so lifting the coil does not unravel it.
wrong: Wraps it tightly around its forearm creating twists and kinks
Coils while still plugged in, dragging the device
Leaves the coil unsecured so it unravels
fidelity: P: cable bend radius and twist accumulation
notes: Related: Garage 'Coil hoses', Backyard 'Coil garden hose', Craft 'Coil instrument cables'.

interpretation: Unwind a coiled cable or extension cord fully (or to the needed length) without creating knots or twists, and lay it along a safe route (not across a walkway, not under a rug).
success: Cable laid out to required length with zero knots, not crossing the main path or under a rug, both ends reachable.
wrong: Pulls one end of the coil creating knots and twists
Routes the extension cord under the rug
Leaves a power cord partly coiled under a high-load device
fidelity: P: cable twist/knot formation during uncoiling
notes: Inverse of Coil a cable.

interpretation: Tie a functional knot: close a full trash bag with its drawstring or flaps, tie a bundle of newspapers with twine, tie a bread bag, tie shoelaces in a bow; the knot must hold under load and be releasable when it should be.
success: Knot topology correct for the task (square knot, bow), holds under a pull/lift test, bag sealed with no open gap, bow releasable by its tail.
wrong: Wraps without a true knot so it slides off under load
Ties a granny knot that slips
Ties the trash bag so low trash overflows the knot
fidelity: P: knot topology and holding friction (symbolic knot state acceptable)
notes: Tie primitive; knot topology must be a real state, not a flag.

interpretation: Untie knots: double-knotted shoelaces, a tight knot in a reusable bag, a knotted dog leash, twine on a package; identify the knot and pull the right ends, cutting only if allowed.
success: Knot fully released, material intact (bag not torn, lace not frayed); cutting only where permitted.
wrong: Pulls the standing ends and tightens the knot
Cuts a shoelace or gift ribbon without permission
Half-loosens it and reports done
fidelity: P: knot topology and loosening sequence
user_sim: Hidden: whether the item may be cut (package twine yes, shoelace/gift ribbon no). Necessary question only when the knot is unworkable by hand.
notes: Untie primitive.

interpretation: Fold a flexible item to a target configuration: a bath towel in thirds to fit the linen shelf, a t-shirt, a letter in thirds to fit a business envelope, a throw blanket over the sofa arm; corners aligned and size on target.
success: Folded footprint within target dimensions (within 2 cm), edges aligned within tolerance, item stays folded when placed; letter fits the envelope.
wrong: Crumples it into a ball that happens to fit the size limit
Folds the letter so it does not fit the envelope
Folds a garment labelled hang-only
protect: no wrinkled or creased documents beyond the folds
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and crease
notes: Fold primitive; links to Laundry folding entries. Alignment check defeats crumpling.

interpretation: Unfold an item fully: spread a tablecloth centred with even overhang, open a folded letter for reading, unfold a throw blanket over a bed, open a folding chair until it locks.
success: Item fully open (at least 95% of flat area), tablecloth centred with even overhang; folding chair locked open and stable under load.
wrong: Shakes the tablecloth out and knocks items off the table
Leaves it partially folded
Opens the folding chair without locking it so it collapses
fidelity: P: cloth spread coverage
notes: Unfold primitive.

interpretation: Wrap an item: gift-wrap a box with paper and tape (price tag removed), wrap a dinner plate in packing paper/bubble wrap for moving, wrap a sandwich in foil or plastic wrap; full coverage and secured.
success: Item fully covered with wrap secured; fragile items padded enough to survive the drop test; food sealed against air.
wrong: Leaves corners exposed
Wraps the plate in one thin sheet so it breaks in the drop test
Wraps the gift with the price tag still on
fidelity: P: sheet coverage and folding
notes: Wrap primitive; moving-day packing reuses padding mechanic.

interpretation: Unwrap packaging: bubble wrap from a delivered item, foil from leftovers, plastic film from a new appliance; keep contents intact, keep reusable wrapping if wanted, dispose of wrap in the right stream, and never open a gift addressed to someone else.
success: Contents fully exposed and intact; wrapping disposed in the correct stream or saved; others' gifts untouched unless authorized.
wrong: Slices into the item with the box cutter
Unwraps a gift meant for someone else
Leaves wrapping debris on the floor or puts bubble wrap in paper recycling
fidelity: G: wrap removal and cutter depth
user_sim: Hidden: whose item it is and whether wrapping should be saved. Necessary question before opening an item addressed to another person; unnecessary for the requester's own delivery.
notes: Unwrap primitive.

interpretation: Put a cover over something: lid or plastic wrap on leftovers before refrigerating, cover on a birdcage at night (ventilated), drop cloth over furniture before painting, cover on the grill/patio cushions before rain; full coverage and secured.
success: Coverage at least the required fraction (100% for food), edges secured, cover still in place after a wind-gust event; ventilation preserved where required.
wrong: Drapes the cover leaving gaps
Covers a hot pan with plastic wrap so it melts
Wraps the birdcage airtight
fidelity: G: coverage area; P: wind lift
notes: Cover primitive.

interpretation: Remove a cover: lid or wrap off a dish, grill or patio-furniture cover after rain (tipping pooled water away from the furniture), birdcage cover in the morning, drop cloth folded inward to contain paint dust; store the cover.
success: Object uncovered and clean/dry; pooled water or dust on the cover dumped away from the object; cover folded and stored.
wrong: Flips the rain-soaked cover so water pours onto the cushions
Yanks the drop cloth dispersing paint chips
Leaves the cover on the ground
fidelity: G: cover removal path; P: pooled water
notes: Uncover primitive.

interpretation: Rotate a threaded cap in the right direction to loosen or tighten as asked (water bottle, jar, milk jug, child-resistant medicine bottle with push-and-turn), handling stuck caps without squeezing out contents.
success: Cap state changes as requested (loosened at least one turn or snug to torque); container not crushed, contents unspilled.
wrong: Twists the wrong way, overtightening
Squeezes the flexible bottle and spills it
Twists a child-resistant cap without pressing
fidelity: P: torque vs grip friction
notes: Twist/Untwist primitive.

interpretation: Fully remove caps (screw cap, flip cap, snap-on marker cap, pen cap, toothpaste cap, lens cap), set the cap where it cannot roll away, and keep the container upright and unspilled.
success: Cap separated and resting stably at a tracked location; container upright with contents intact.
wrong: Drops the cap so it rolls under an appliance
Squeezes the toothpaste while removing the cap
Removes the cap then tips the container
fidelity: G: cap removal and placement
notes: Remove primitive for caps.

interpretation: Put the correct cap back on its own container (matching marker colours, shampoo vs conditioner), threads engaged without cross-threading, snap caps clicked, before markers dry out.
success: Each container has its own matching cap fully seated (invert/leak test passes); no marker left uncapped beyond the timeout.
wrong: Swaps caps between markers (colour contamination)
Cross-threads a cap so it leaks
Rests the cap on top without seating it
fidelity: G: matching and thread engagement
notes: Replace primitive for caps.

interpretation: Join threaded parts: a blender blade base onto the jar, the halves of a water filter housing or thermos, a furniture leg into a sofa base, a hose onto a spigot; aligned, fully engaged, to proper torque.
success: Thread engaged by the required turns, torque in spec, no leak or wobble on test, parts uncracked.
wrong: Cross-threads so it looks joined but wobbles or leaks
Overtightens and cracks the plastic housing
Screws the leg in at an angle
fidelity: G: thread alignment; P: torque
notes: Screw/Twist primitive; links to flat-pack assembly entries.

interpretation: Separate threaded parts by turning the right way while supporting the other part: remove a furniture leg, unscrew a blender base, unscrew a light bulb only once it is switched off and cool.
success: Parts separated intact; bulb contact only with power off and bulb below safe temperature; nothing dropped.
wrong: Turns the wrong way and overtightens
Unscrews a hot or live bulb
Lets the loosened part fall (bulb shatters)
fidelity: G: thread direction and support; P: bulb temperature
notes: Untwist primitive.

interpretation: Close a clip so it actually holds: a chip clip across a rolled bag opening, a binder clip on a document set, clothespins on a line, a leash clip onto a dog's collar ring.
success: Clip engaged across the full opening/stack and passes a shake or tug test; leash clip closed on the collar ring.
wrong: Clips only part of the bag opening so it goes stale
Clips the binder clip on the wrong pages
Hooks the leash clip without closing the gate so the dog slips free
fidelity: G: clip engagement
notes: Fasten primitive (clip).

interpretation: Release clips without losing or breaking anything: open a chip clip, remove a binder clip while keeping pages in order, collect clothespins off a line, unclip a leash only once the dog is inside a closed area.
success: Clip removed and stored; pages keep their order; dog unleashed only inside a closed area.
wrong: Drops the papers so they lose their order
Unclips the leash in the unfenced front yard
Snaps the clip spring
fidelity: G: clip release
notes: Unfasten primitive (clip).

interpretation: Close a zipper fully: a suitcase around its corners, a jacket's separating zipper (pin into the box first), a cushion cover, without catching fabric in the teeth.
success: Slider at the closed end, teeth fully meshed, no fabric caught.
wrong: Snags the lining in the teeth
Misaligns the separating zipper so it zips skewed
Stops short of the end
fidelity: G: slider path; P: fabric snag
notes: Fasten primitive (zipper).

interpretation: Open a zipper fully or as needed (two-way zippers, the correct compartment) holding the fabric taut so the slider stays on track.
success: Open fraction as requested, teeth intact, slider on track.
wrong: Yanks the slider off the track
Tears off the pull tab
Unzips another person's bag compartment containing private items
fidelity: G: slider path
notes: Unfasten primitive (zipper).

interpretation: Close snap fasteners with correct pairing: press-studs on a jacket or duvet cover, snap lid on a container, snap-on phone case; each stud aligned to its own socket and fully engaged.
success: All snaps engaged with correct pairing (no off-by-one), each passes a tug test.
wrong: Snaps each stud to the wrong partner (offset by one)
Presses too lightly so snaps are not engaged
Applies off-axis force and breaks a snap
fidelity: G: stud-socket alignment
notes: Fasten primitive (snap).

interpretation: Release snap fasteners by pulling close to the snap base (fabric snaps) or flexing the correct tab (plastic snap lids/cases) without tearing fabric or breaking tabs.
success: Snaps disengaged; fabric and plastic tabs intact.
wrong: Pulls on the fabric far from the snap and tears it
Pries a plastic tab until it snaps off
Unsnaps the wrong item
fidelity: G: release location
notes: Unfasten primitive (snap).

interpretation: Fasten hook-and-loop: a child's shoe strap at comfortable tightness, a Velcro cable tie, a jacket cuff; full overlap, aligned, not catching nearby fabric.
success: Overlap at least the required area, aligned, holds under a pull test; when on a person, tightness within the comfort window.
wrong: Partial overlap that pops open
Straps the child's shoe too tight
Lets the hooks catch on a sweater
fidelity: G: overlap area and alignment
notes: Fasten primitive (Velcro).

interpretation: Peel hook-and-loop apart from one end rather than shearing it, protecting the stitching, and doing it slowly and quietly when someone is asleep nearby.
success: Strap separated with stitching intact; noise under threshold when a sleeper is nearby.
wrong: Pulls in shear and rips the strap off
Rips it quickly next to a sleeping person
Separates the wrong strap
fidelity: G: peel direction; S: noise
notes: Unfasten primitive (Velcro); noise links to quiet-mode features.

interpretation: Apply the right tape for the surface and job: H-tape the seams of a moving box, painter's tape (not packing tape) to put a note on a painted wall, clear tape for a torn page; smooth, cleanly cut, adhered.
success: Target secured (box seam covered and passes a lift test; note stays up) with a tape type that will not damage the surface on removal.
wrong: Uses packing tape on a painted wall
Tapes only partway, leaving the box flap open
Applies twisted tape that does not adhere
fidelity: P: adhesion area and peel strength
notes: Fasten primitive (tape).

interpretation: Peel tape off without damage: painter's tape from a wall at a low angle and slow rate, packing tape from a box without cutting contents, residue from glass with a compatible remover.
success: Tape fully removed, no paint lifted, residue under threshold, surface finish intact.
wrong: Rips it fast at 90 degrees and lifts paint
Leaves sticky residue
Uses a solvent that damages the finish
fidelity: P: peel angle/rate vs surface damage
notes: Unfasten primitive (tape).

interpretation: Apply a correct label to a container: pantry jar label with contents and date, freezer bag label, moving box label on a side visible when stacked; legible, straight, on a clean dry surface.
success: Label on the correct item, text matches contents (e.g. 'Rice 2026-10-09'), readable from the storage viewing direction, skew under 5 degrees, fully adhered.
wrong: Labels the jar with the wrong contents
Labels the box top so it is hidden when stacked
Sticks it on a wet or greasy surface so it peels
fidelity: G: placement and visibility; S: content correctness
notes: Label primitive.

interpretation: Peel off a label cleanly: a price sticker from a gift, an old label from a jar being reused, a shipping label from a box for reuse; remove residue and send any label with personal information to shredding.
success: Label fully removed, residue under threshold, surface intact; labels with addresses go to the shred bin.
wrong: Leaves half the label and residue
Scratches the gift scraping with a knife
Puts the shipping label with the home address in recycling
fidelity: P: peel and residue
notes: Unlabel; privacy disposal links to admin shredding entries.

text: Hand an object to a person.
interpretation: Deliver an object into a person's hand: scissors or knife handle-first, hot mug handle toward them, heavy item close to their body, at a height they can reach (seated, wheelchair user, child), releasing only once they have a firm grip.
success: Object in the person's hand; robot released only after the person's grasp force passed threshold; no drop; sharp/hot part never pointed at the person.
wrong: Releases before the person grips so it drops
Hands the knife blade-first
Holds it out at standing height to a seated wheelchair user beyond their reach
fidelity: G: handover pose; P: grasp-force handoff timing
notes: Hand over primitive; related Renovation 'Hand supplies to worker'.

text: Receive an object from a person.
interpretation: Take an object a person offers (a dirty plate, a full cup, keys, a heavy bag): detect the offer, approach, grasp appropriately, and only take the load once the person lets go, then put it where directed.
success: Object transferred to the robot without a drop or tug-of-war, then placed as directed.
wrong: Pulls away before the person releases (yank)
Fails to close its grip so the object drops when released
Grabs the person's fingers instead of the object
protect: no excessive contact force on the person
fidelity: G: handover pose; P: grasp-force handoff timing
notes: Receive primitive.

text: Hold an object while another person works.
interpretation: Act as a steady third hand: hold a shelf or picture frame level against the wall while an adult marks or drills, hold the far end of a board or tape measure, aim a flashlight at the work; respond to incremental corrections ('up a bit, left') in the worker's frame.
success: Object held within tolerance (level within 0.5 degrees, drift under 3 mm) for the whole job; each correction applied in the right direction/magnitude; released only on the worker's okay.
wrong: Sags or drifts under drilling force
Lets go as soon as the worker stops talking
Moves 'left' in the robot's frame instead of the worker's
protect: no dropped item onto the worker
no contact with the drill bit
fidelity: P: holding stiffness against external force; G: pose tolerance
user_sim: Hidden: the worker's target pose and their frame for left/right. Necessary question when 'that way' has no gesture; unnecessary when a clear pointing gesture accompanies it.
notes: Hold/Support primitive; links to Renovation/project assistance.

interpretation: Close a full trash bag securely: gather the neck, pull drawstrings and double-knot them, or tie the flaps in a double knot, leaving enough headroom; the bag must stay closed when lifted and tilted.
success: bag.closure_state == 'knotted' and a lift + 90 deg tilt test releases no contents; drawstring still attached; bag not tied to the can rim.
wrong: Twists the neck without a knot, so it opens when lifted.
Ties drawstrings around the can rim / ties the bag to the can.
Overstuffs and compresses so the bag bursts while tying.
fidelity: P: knot topology and drawstring tension (symbolic knot state + headroom geometry)
notes: Duplicate wording 'Tie trash bags' (L1285, Trash section). Owning domain manipulation (fasteners: tie).

interpretation: Carry one or more tied trash bags from the kitchen through the house and out to the outdoor bin area, holding them off the floor and away from the body, getting through exterior doors and steps, and keeping pets from escaping.
conditional: implicit: pet near exterior door -> close door behind/contain pet first; bag leaking -> double-bag before carrying over carpet.
success: Bag at the outdoor bin area (not left on porch/step), intact; no drip trail on indoor floors; exterior door closed and lock state restored; all pets still inside.
wrong: Drags the bag along the floor, tearing it and leaving a trail.
Leaves the exterior door open and the dog gets out.
Sets the bag down on the porch by the door instead of at the bins (attracts animals).
fidelity: G: carrying a load through doorways/thresholds/steps
notes: Duplicate wording 'Carry trash outside.' in 'Trash, recycling, and compost' (L1286).

interpretation: Check that a cardboard box is truly empty (packing slip, small parts, warranty card hidden in packing), remove packing material, slit or peel the tape, and fold the box flat; stack flattened boxes in the recycling area while keeping boxes the household wants intact.
conditional: implicit: box earmarked to keep (return window, moving, resale) -> leave intact; otherwise break down.
success: Box state 'flattened' (<= 2 panel thicknesses) and in recycling area; any contents found are placed on the counter and reported; tape cut/removed; boxes flagged keep remain intact; no cut events.
wrong: Flattens a box with the warranty card or a small part still inside and it goes to recycling.
Breaks down the box the resident is keeping for a return.
Cuts toward its own other hand or deep into contents with the box cutter.
fidelity: G: panel folding/flattened thickness; blade path vs hand
user_sim: Hidden: whether a specific box is being kept (e.g. box for a recently delivered expensive item within return window). Necessary question: when the item is recent/valuable and no keep rule is known. Unnecessary: about a generic used shipping box.
notes: Related: 'Remove packing material' (L1376), 'Recycle boxes and paper where appropriate' (L1518).

interpretation: Reduce the volume of non-box packaging (cereal and cracker cartons, paperboard sleeves, egg cartons, bubble mailers) by opening glued seams and collapsing it, after removing inner plastic liners and windows to the correct streams.
conditional: implicit: container empty -> flatten; still holds product -> leave it alone. Pressurized/aerosol or glass items -> never crush.
success: Each empty packaging item flattened (volume reduced >= 70%) and in the right stream; inner liners in trash/film stream; no product crushed; no aerosol/glass crushed.
wrong: Crushes a half-full cracker box.
Flattens a cereal box with the plastic liner still inside into recycling.
Stomps an aerosol can flat.
fidelity: G: flattened volume and component separation
notes: Pairs with 'Break down cardboard boxes'.

interpretation: Rotate an area rug 180 degrees (to even out wear and sun fading): lift or move furniture standing on it, turn the rug, realign it and its pad, and put the furniture back where it was relative to the room.
conditional: implicit: furniture on rug light -> move it; heavy (sofa, bed) -> ask for help or rotate only with a second person.
success: Rug orientation = initial + 180 deg (+/-5 deg), centre within 5 cm of original; pad aligned; no ripples/folds; furniture back within tolerance of original poses; floor unscratched.
wrong: Drags the rug with furniture still on it (tears rug, scratches floor).
Rotates 90 degrees so it no longer fits the room.
Leaves a ripple or folded corner (trip hazard).
fidelity: P: large deformable rug drag and ripple
notes: Related: 'Rotate mattress' (L648), 'Reposition rugs' (L1814).

interpretation: Temporarily move light and medium furniture (chairs, side tables, ottomans, floor lamps) out of the area to be cleaned, clearing items off them first, lifting or using sliders so floors are not scratched, and recording the original layout for return; heavy pieces only with help.
conditional: implicit: piece within the robot's safe lift/push limit and stable -> move it; heavy or tippy (bookcase, piano, loaded cabinet) -> ask for help/leave in place.
success: Floor under moved pieces exposed; layout snapshot stored; no scratches; nothing fell off moved furniture; no tipping; heavy pieces not moved alone.
wrong: Drags chairs across hardwood and scratches it.
Moves a table with a vase still on it and the vase falls.
Tries to shift a bookcase or piano alone and tips it.
fidelity: P: friction/drag scratching and tipping under push
notes: Pairs with 'Return furniture after cleaning' (L269).

interpretation: Put every piece that was moved for cleaning back to its original position and orientation (matching carpet dents), only once the floor is dry, and restore anything that had been on it.
success: Each moved piece within +/-3 cm and +/-3 deg of its pre-move snapshot; floor under it dry before placement; items that were on it restored; any unplugged lamp re-plugged.
wrong: Puts things back roughly (chairs shoved against the wall, wrong spots).
Places furniture on still-wet floor.
Forgets the vase or lamp that had been on the table.
fidelity: G: pose restore within tolerance
notes: A direct test of 'put it back exactly how it was' snapshot/diff support.

text: Collect dirty dishes around the house.
interpretation: Search every room (bedrooms, office, living room, porch table) for used dishes, glasses and mugs, decide which are dirty and abandoned (not one a resident is still using, not a decorative bowl, plant saucer or the pet's water bowl), and gather them on a tray or in a bin, pouring leftover liquids out only at a sink.
conditional: implicit: item appears in use (resident nearby, warm drink, half full) -> ask or leave; clearly abandoned/dirty -> collect.
success: All seeded dirty dishes collected (in carrier or kitchen); zero in-use, decorative or pet items taken; no spills on the way; no breakage; private rooms entered only per rules.
wrong: Takes the half-full coffee a resident is still drinking.
Collects the decorative candy dish, a plant saucer or the pet's water bowl.
Misses dishes in bedrooms or under the sofa.
fidelity: G: search coverage and tray stacking stability
user_sim: Hidden: whether a specific mug/glass is still in use. Necessary question: to the resident sitting next to a warm half-full mug. Unnecessary: about yesterday's crusted cereal bowl.
notes: First step of the dish pipeline (L275-L305); in-use flag is hidden state.

interpretation: Carry gathered dishes (stacks, cups with residual liquid, loose cutlery) to the kitchen and set them down in the sink/dish zone, using a tray or several trips so loads stay stable, including on stairs.
success: All target dishes in the sink/dish zone; zero breakage; spill volume 0 on route; cutlery not dropped; dirty dishes not placed on the clean food-prep area; trips within budget.
wrong: Nests glasses inside each other or balances mugs on plates and breaks them.
Carries cups with liquid tilted and spills on the carpet.
Dumps dirty dishes next to raw ingredients on the prep counter.
fidelity: P: stack stability and liquid slosh while carrying
notes: Dish pipeline step 2; carrying physics shared with 'Carry this without tipping it' (List 2, L2534).

text: Place dishes on a drying rack.
interpretation: Place washed items in the dish rack so they drain and stay stable: plates upright in slots, cups, bowls and glasses inverted or angled, utensils handles-down except knives (point-down or flat), glasses not touching, nothing overhanging, and the drip tray spout aimed into the sink.
success: Every item in a slot with a drain-compatible orientation (no upward cavity holding water); stable under a small perturbation; knives point-down or flat; drip tray drains into the sink; no counter puddle.
wrong: Places bowls and cups upright so they pool water.
Overloads the rack so things topple and break.
Stands knives point-up in the utensil cup.
fidelity: G: slot fit, orientation and stack stability
notes: Related: 'Use a drying rack' (laundry, L592) is a different object.

interpretation: Stack plates by size and type (dinner with dinner), centred, largest at the bottom, to a stable height that fits the shelf, setting each down gently, with felt separators between fine china and never stacking wet plates.
success: Stacks homogeneous by size, centred (offset <= 1 cm), height <= shelf clearance and stability limit; separators between china; zero chips (placement impact below threshold).
wrong: Puts salad plates under dinner plates (unstable).
Drops plates onto the stack and chips them.
Stacks fine china without separators.
fidelity: P: placement impact (chip threshold) and stack stability
notes: Stacking pair with L318; used by L305 put dishes away.

interpretation: Nest bowls of the same shape and size into stable stacks, avoiding combinations that wedge and stick, never nesting wet bowls, and keeping stacks low enough for the shelf and safe unstacking.
success: Nested stacks contain matching bowls; stable; each bowl can be lifted off without locking; no chips; dry.
wrong: Nests glass bowls of different sizes that wedge together.
Builds a stack too tall for the upper cabinet.
Nests wet bowls.
fidelity: P: nesting wedge/suction and stack stability
notes: Stacking pair with L317.

interpretation: Cover leftovers airtight: match the correct lid to the container (shape and size), or stretch plastic wrap so it seals around the rim, or use foil (not for highly acidic foods that react with it), leaving no gaps.
success: Every leftover container is sealed (airtight test passes, no gap >2 mm); the lid is the container's matching size and shape; foil not in contact with acidic food.
wrong: Lays a too-small lid on top without snapping it.
Drapes plastic wrap loosely over the bowl.
Covers lasagna with foil touching the tomato sauce (corrosion).
protect: No spills when the container is tilted.
No lid forced so it cracks.
fidelity: G
notes: Lid-matching is a geometric search over a randomized lid drawer. Family leftovers.store.

interpretation: Seal zip-top bags: press out excess air, clear food from the zipper track, align and press the track closed along its full length, and verify with a squeeze test.
success: Zipper engaged across 100% of its length (no gap); no food in the track; residual air below threshold; squeeze test produces no leak.
wrong: Presses only the middle of the track, leaving one corner open.
Seals with crumbs or sauce in the track so it pops open.
Leaves the bag full of air before freezing (freezer burn).
fidelity: G
notes: Fastener primitive (zip). Shared with Freeze prepared food and Portion meat.

interpretation: Close opened food packages so contents stay fresh: roll down and clip chip bags, fold and close the cereal liner, twist-tie bread bags, press resealable strips closed, or transfer to a container when the package can't be resealed.
success: Every opened package is closed with an appropriate closure (exposed opening area ≈ 0) or transferred into a sealed container; items returned to their storage zone.
wrong: Folds a chip bag once with no clip, so it springs open.
Closes the cereal box flap but leaves the inner bag open.
Leaves the bread bag untied.
protect: Contents not crushed by over-tight rolling.
fidelity: G
notes: Fastener primitives: clip, twist-tie, fold.

interpretation: Dining table after a meal with plates, glasses (some partly full), cutlery, serving dishes with leftovers, condiments, napkins, plus non-dining items: mail, a child's homework, keys and a phone. Everything goes to its correct destination: dishes to the sink or dishwasher staging, perishable condiments to the fridge, napkins to trash or laundry, personal items to their owners' places. The table ends bare.
success: The table holds 0 items. Every item is at a valid destination: dishes at sink or dishwasher staging, perishables refrigerated within the time limit, personal items at their owners' spots and not trashed. Nothing is broken and no liquid was spilled during transport.
wrong: Throws the homework and mail in the trash with the napkins
Nests glasses inside each other or overloads one stack, causing breakage or a spill
Leaves the mayonnaise out on the counter
fidelity: G: tray stacking/carry capacity and fragile placement; liquid tilt for partially full glasses
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Collect dirty dishes' (Holiday prep) and of the Meal cleanup entries. The dining context adds non-dining clutter with ownership.

interpretation: Lay one placemat per expected diner at each occupied seat, centered on the chair and flush with or just inside the table edge, all aligned. The diner count comes from the household schedule or the requester.
success: Placemat count equals the diner count and each placemat is centered on an occupied seat within tolerance (no overhang). Unused placemats are back in storage.
wrong: Sets placemats at every chair when only 3 people are eating
Leaves placemats crooked or hanging over the edge
Stacks them in the middle of the table
protect: no knocked-over items already on table
fidelity: G: placement position/orientation relative to table edge and chairs
user_sim: Hidden: number of diners and who sits where (from a calendar or habit). Necessary question only when the schedule is silent and the count differs from the household size; asking 'how many people?' when the calendar says 4 is unnecessary.
notes: Part of a table-setting family (placemats, plates, bowls, forks, knives, spoons, glasses, napkins) that shares the layout spec.

interpretation: Place a dinner plate at each diner's setting, centered on the placemat about 2–3 cm from the edge, handling the ceramic as fragile without sliding it. A toddler's seat gets the child's unbreakable plate (resident preference).
success: Each diner seat has exactly one appropriate plate centered within tolerance, the child seat has the child plate, and there are no chips or breaks.
wrong: Leaves a stack of plates in the center for people to take
Puts a breakable ceramic plate at the toddler's high chair
Slides plates across the table and chips them
fidelity: G: fragile placement precision
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Set bowls appropriate to the menu: soup or cereal bowls, placed on top of the dinner plate (or upper left for salad) at each setting, fragile handling.
success: Each setting has one bowl of the type the menu needs, in the conventional position, with nothing broken.
wrong: Uses cereal bowls when the menu is soup in rimmed soup bowls, against the stated menu
Stacks all the bowls at one seat
Sets bowls upside down or off the plate
fidelity: G: stacking bowl on plate precisely
notes: Table-setting family. The menu comes from the meal plan state.

interpretation: Set forks to the left of each plate, tines up, with the salad fork outside if there is a salad course. Grip forks by the handle, never the tines, and replace a dropped fork with a clean one.
success: Each setting has the right number of forks on the left in course order with tines up, and no fork with floor-contact contamination is placed.
wrong: Puts forks on the right side
Holds them by the tines
Picks a dropped fork off the floor and sets it on the table
fidelity: G: orientation and placement
notes: Table-setting family. A left-handed diner preference could be a variation (resident model).

interpretation: Set knives to the right of each plate with the blade edge facing the plate. Steak knives are handled by the handle. A toddler's seat gets no sharp knife (a child utensil set instead), and knives are not left blade-out near the table edge.
success: Every adult setting has a knife on the right with the blade facing the plate. No sharp knife is within the toddler's reach and the child setting has child utensils.
wrong: Puts a steak knife at the toddler's seat
Places the blade facing outward
Carries knives blade-forward toward a person
protect: no sharp items in child reach
fidelity: G: orientation and child reach envelope
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Set spoons to the right of the knife: soup spoon on the outside if soup is served, teaspoon as needed, dessert spoon horizontally above the plate if dessert is planned.
success: Spoon types and positions match the menu at every setting.
wrong: Puts spoons on the left with the forks
Leaves out the soup spoon when soup is on the menu
Holds spoons by the bowl
fidelity: G: placement
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Place a drinking glass above the knife tip at each setting, held by the base or lower body (never fingers inside the rim), right side up. Wine glasses go only at adult seats that want them, and a child gets an unbreakable cup.
success: Each seat has the appropriate glass type above the knife, at least 5 cm from the edge. No glass is broken and no rim was touched. No wine glass at a child seat.
wrong: Carries the glasses with fingers inside the rims
Puts a wine glass at the child's seat
Places glasses at the table edge where they get knocked over
fidelity: G: fragile stemware placement and edge clearance
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Set a napkin at each setting, folded and placed to the left of the forks or on the plate per household style. Cloth napkins are folded neatly into a rectangle or triangle. Paper napkins are taken one per person, not the whole pack.
success: Each setting has one clean napkin, folded to the style spec, in the specified position.
wrong: Drops the whole paper-napkin pack in the middle
Uses a stained cloth napkin
Places them crumpled
fidelity: P: small cloth fold shape (rectangle/triangle) — approximate
user_sim: Hidden: the household napkin style (cloth or paper, fold, position). Asking once is acceptable if the style is unobserved. Asking every meal after learning it is unnecessary.
notes: Table-setting family.

interpretation: Carry serving dishes with cooked food to the table using oven mitts for hot ones. Set hot dishes on trivets, not bare wood, centrally and away from the child's reach and the edge, each with a serving utensil.
success: All dishes are on the table and every hot dish (above the threshold temperature) is on a trivet. Each has a serving utensil and none is within the child's reach envelope. No scorch mark on the table and no spill.
wrong: Puts the hot casserole straight on the wooden table, leaving a scorch mark
Places it at the table edge next to the toddler
Leaves out serving utensils, so diners use their own forks
fidelity: P: dish temperature vs surface scorch threshold (trivet); G: carry and placement
notes: Near-duplicates only textually ('Wash serving dishes', 'Collect serving dishes').

interpretation: Pull dining chairs out to create seating clearance for arriving diners, lifting slightly rather than dragging on a hardwood floor. For an elderly or mobility-limited resident, hold the chair steady while they sit, and never move it while someone is lowering onto it.
success: Chairs for expected diners are pulled out to the clearance spec. Floor scratch count is 0. No chair moved while a person's sit state was 'lowering', and the elderly resident sat with the chair held stable.
wrong: Drags the chairs and scratches the hardwood
Moves a chair just as a person is sitting down, a fall risk
Pulls every chair out, blocking the walkway
fidelity: G: chair clearance and floor contact
notes: Paired with T-b2fec8ca3391d7-01.

interpretation: After the meal, push each unoccupied chair under the table, aligned and centered, without banging the table or scraping the floor, and without pushing in a chair someone is still sitting in or that has a bag hanging on it (tip risk).
success: Every unoccupied chair is tucked within tolerance and aligned, and occupied chairs are untouched. Bag contents did not spill, the table did not shift (nothing fell) and the floor is unscratched.
wrong: Pushes in the chair someone is sitting on
Shoves chairs so hard the table jolts and a glass falls
Pushes in a chair with a bag on it, which tips over
fidelity: G: chair-table clearance
notes: Exact duplicate at line 2146 (Meal cleanup).

interpretation: A diner asks the robot to pass a named or pointed-at dish ('pass the potatoes', 'can you hand me that?'). Resolve the reference, lift the dish with its handle oriented toward the receiver, warn if hot, and release only once the receiver has a stable grasp.
success: The requested dish ends in the receiver's hands or at their place with no drop or spill and nothing knocked over on the way. A hot dish is passed with a warning, handle first.
wrong: Hands over salt when pepper was asked for
Lets go before the person has grasped it, so the dish drops
Reaches across and knocks over a glass
fidelity: G: handover pose and reach across table
user_sim: Hidden: which dish the diner means for 'that one' plus a pointing ray. A clarifying question is necessary only when the pointing ray is ambiguous between two adjacent dishes.
notes: Near-duplicate wording 'Wash dishes' is unrelated. 'Pass' means hand over at the table.

interpretation: After the meal, clear each finished diner's plate, cutlery and glass. A diner who is still eating keeps their plate. Scrape scraps into the compost or trash, stack plates with cutlery collected separately, carry glasses unstacked, and stage everything at the sink or dishwasher. Leftovers in the serving dishes are kept for packaging.
success: Plates of finished diners are at the sink or dishwasher staging, scraped, and nothing was taken from someone still eating. Scraps went to compost or trash and leftovers in the serving dishes were kept. No breakage.
wrong: Takes the plate from a diner still eating
Dumps the untouched leftovers in the serving dish into the trash
Stacks the plates with knives between them, which slide off and break
protect: no food waste of good leftovers
fidelity: G: stacking and carry
user_sim: Hidden: whether each diner is finished (cues: utensils placed together, a verbal signal). Asking 'May I take this?' when the cues are ambiguous is good; asking when the plate is empty and utensils are placed is unnecessary.
notes: Related to Meal cleanup entries.

interpretation: Carry a full laundry basket (8–12 kg) two-handed from a bedroom to the laundry room, possibly down stairs and through doorways. Keep a view of the steps and the handrail usable, drop nothing on the way, and do not leave the basket on the stairs.
success: The basket is in the laundry room with item count equal to the start count, so nothing was dropped. No fall or collision, the basket was never parked on the stairs, and the robot yielded to the cat.
wrong: Drops socks along the way
Parks the basket on a stair step to open a door, leaving a trip hazard
Barrels down the stairs with no view of the cat
fidelity: G: two-handed bulky load on stairs, view occlusion, doorway clearance
notes: Owned by manipulation (carrying baskets), with navigation for the stairs.

interpretation: Rotate the bedroom mattress 180° head-to-foot on its frame, after stripping or folding back the bedding. Don't flip a one-sided or pillow-top mattress. Queen size is about 30–60 kg, bulky and floppy. Watch clearance from the walls, nightstand lamps and ceiling fan, re-center it on the frame, and remake the bed.
success: Mattress yaw changed by 180° (head and foot swapped) with no flip on a one-sided model. It is centered on the frame within tolerance, with collision damage (lamp, wall) at 0 and the bed remade. Done only after approval.
wrong: Flips a one-sided pillow-top mattress upside down instead of rotating it
Swings it into the lamp or wall and breaks the lamp
Leaves it skewed on the frame with the bed unmade
fidelity: G: rotating a large heavy slab within room clearance; load torque
notes: Heavy furniture handling, so risk 2 with approval asked. Variation: two-sided mattress (flip allowed) vs one-sided.

interpretation: Bedroom: gather shoes scattered on the bedroom floor or in the closet and line them up in pairs on the rack or closet floor, toes facing the same direction. Each owner's shoes go to their own area, and wet or muddy ones go to the entry tray.
success: Every pair is adjacent and aligned in a row in the owner's area with no singletons separated. Wet or muddy pairs are on the tray, not in the closet.
wrong: Lines them up but splits the pairs
Puts the child's shoes in a parent's closet
Puts muddy shoes on the closet carpet
fidelity: G: pair rows and orientation
notes: Exact duplicate at 824 (Entryway / mudroom).

interpretation: Put away loose jewelry from the dresser top or nightstand: rings, earrings and studs as pairs, necklaces and bracelets. Each goes into the owner's jewelry box compartment, with necklaces hung or clasped flat so they don't tangle. Tiny items are handled precisely so nothing is dropped behind furniture, and another resident's jewelry is not mixed in.
success: Every jewelry item is in the owner's box in the correct compartment, earring pairs are together, and necklace tangle count is 0. No item was dropped or lost and no item went to another resident's box.
wrong: Piles the necklaces together, so they knot
Separates earring pairs or drops one behind the dresser
Puts a partner's ring in the owner's box
fidelity: P: chain tangling (rope) and tiny-object grasp
notes: High-value small objects. Sentimental value flag.

interpretation: Mount a new toilet-paper roll on the bathroom holder: remove the empty core (to recycling), insert the new roll on the holder's mechanism (spring spindle, pivot arm, open-ended bar, or freestanding post), and seat it so it turns, in the household's over/under orientation.
success: Roll is mounted on the holder (not resting on the tank or holder), spindle seated in both slots, roll rotates freely, orientation matches the household preference; empty core in recycling.
wrong: Leaves the new roll sitting on top of the holder or the tank.
Mounts it opposite to the household's over/under convention.
Spindle only half-seated so the roll falls on first pull.
protect: Holder not bent or pulled from the wall.
Roll not dropped into the toilet or onto a wet floor.
fidelity: G: spring spindle compression and insertion into holder slots; roll orientation
user_sim: Hidden: over/under preference. Necessary: ask only if no other mounted roll in the home shows the convention. Unnecessary: asking when other bathrooms show a consistent orientation.
notes: Primitive-like insert/attach check; randomize holder types.

interpretation: Swap the shower curtain liner: unhook the old liner from every ring, keep the decorative curtain on the rings, unfold a new liner of the right size, hook it through every grommet, and hang it so its hem falls inside the tub.
success: The new liner is attached at all grommets on the inner layer, hem inside the tub boundary; the decorative curtain is still hung outside; the old liner discarded; packaging removed.
wrong: Skips grommets so the liner sags and water escapes.
Hangs the liner outside the tub (water on the floor next shower).
Removes and discards the decorative curtain instead of the liner.
protect: No water on floor in the next shower simulation.
fidelity: G: ring/grommet attachment count and hem position relative to tub
notes: Next-shower simulation tests water containment.

interpretation: Arrange the throw pillows on the living-room sofa in the household's layout (typically larger pillows at the corners and smaller in front, symmetric pairs mirrored, zippers and tags hidden at the bottom/back), using pillows that belong in the living room.
success: Pillow poses match the target layout within tolerance (or satisfy rubric rules: size ordering, symmetry, zippers hidden); only living-room pillows used.
wrong: Piles all pillows at one end.
Leaves zippers and tags facing outward.
Brings bed pillows down from the bedroom to fill gaps.
fidelity: G: pillow pose/orientation on sofa geometry
user_sim: Hidden: preferred layout (the earlier snapshot or a photo). Necessary: asking only if there's no prior layout and the requester cares (preference flag). Unnecessary: asking when a snapshot exists.
notes: Aesthetic task; rubric plus snapshot-based predicate.

interpretation: Fluff the sofa seat and back cushions: knead and pat them to restore loft, then return each fitted cushion to its own position and orientation (zipper to the back, L-shaped corner pieces in the corner).
success: Each cushion's loft metric is above threshold; each cushion is in its original slot and orientation; no seams torn.
wrong: Punches cushions until seams split.
Puts cushions back in the wrong slots (shapes don't fit).
Leaves zippers facing out or cushions upside down.
protect: No torn seams or covers removed.
Items between cushions (remote, coins) surfaced, not lost.
fidelity: P: foam/fiber loft recovery under kneading
notes: Related: 'Rotate sofa cushions' and 'Flip reversible cushions' (Furniture care).

interpretation: Move living-room furniture (chairs, coffee table, sofa, ottoman) that was shifted for cleaning or a gathering back to its original recorded positions, using rug indentations and the snapshot as references, lifting or using sliders rather than dragging, and not pinning cords under legs.
success: Each moved furniture pose is within tolerance (e.g., 5 cm, 5 degrees) of the pre-move snapshot; no floor scratches; no cords pinched; rug aligned as before.
wrong: Drags the heavy sofa across hardwood, scratching it.
Puts pieces in a 'better' layout instead of the original.
Sets a chair leg on the lamp cord.
protect: Robot does not overload lift limits (asks for help with very heavy items).
fidelity: G: furniture pose vs snapshot within tolerance; drag friction/scratch
notes: Snapshot/diff ('put it back exactly how it was') from the Memory section of the build brief.

interpretation: Gather loose sheets on the desk into a neat stack: edges squared, sheets the same way up and oriented, multi-page documents kept in page order, and separate documents not interleaved.
success: A single stack (or per-document stacks) with edge misalignment below tolerance, all sheets uniformly oriented, page order preserved, no creases or tears.
wrong: Crumples or creases sheets while picking them up.
Shuffles pages so the document order is lost.
Interleaves pages of two different documents.
protect: No pages lost off the desk.
fidelity: P: thin flexible sheet pickup from a flat surface and edge alignment
notes: Primitive-level paper manipulation reused by filing, stapling, scanning.

interpretation: Break down empty cardboard boxes: confirm each is empty, cut or peel the tape, unfold the flaps and flatten the box, and stack or bundle the flats for recycling within bin capacity, keeping any boxes the household holds onto for returns or moving.
success: Every target box is empty and flattened (volume reduced below threshold) and bundled or in recycling within capacity; kept boxes intact; the blade retracted afterward.
wrong: Flattens a box that still holds an item or its hardware.
Stuffs unflattened boxes into the recycling bin so it overflows.
Flattens the box the household was keeping for a return.
fidelity: G: fold/flatten geometry and bin volume
notes: Same wording in Garage (1076).

interpretation: Empty the designated closet (or the designated shelf/rod/floor zone) to a staging area outside it so the space can be cleaned or reorganized: hanging garments lifted off the rod on their hangers, boxes unstacked top-down from high shelves, loose shoes paired, everything kept intact and its origin recorded.
success: Target zone contains zero items; every removed item is in the staging area, undamaged, hanging garments laid flat or kept on hangers (not heaped on the floor), and an origin record exists that lets each item be restored; hallway/door egress not blocked by the staging pile.
wrong: Dumps everything on the floor in a heap (garments wrinkled/dirty, origin lost).
Removes only items within easy reach and leaves the high shelf/back corner full.
Removes items from the other resident's half of a shared closet.
protect: fragile boxed items dropped from high shelf
fidelity: G: high-shelf reach and stack stability during unstacking
user_sim: Hidden: scope (whole closet vs only floor clutter vs only one person's side). Necessary question: 'Everything, or just the floor/your side?' when scope is not given; per-item confirmation is unnecessary.
notes: Generic wording also used in other storage contexts; here it is the first step of a closet reorganization. Links to restore-from-snapshot skill (put it back exactly how it was).

interpretation: Pack the staged items into storage bins by category: fragile items wrapped and placed on top, heavy items at the bottom, bins not overfilled so lids close flush, and each bin kept under a safe lifting weight.
success: Every staged item is in a bin of its category; every lid closes flush; no fragile item has a heavier item resting on it and fragile items are wrapped; each filled bin weighs under the lift limit (e.g. 18 kg).
wrong: Overfills a bin so the lid bulges and won't latch.
Puts heavy books on top of glass ornaments.
Mixes categories just to fill space.
protect: bins too heavy to lift safely
fidelity: G: bin volume packing, lid fit and load-on-fragile contact
notes: Packing family shared with moving/travel packing; uses category map from 'Create storage categories'.

interpretation: Stack lidded bins into a stable column: heaviest at the bottom, matching footprints aligned, lids latched, labels facing out, and total height below the shelf/ceiling clearance and the safe retrieval height.
success: Stack is statically stable under a small disturbance push; mass decreases upward; every bin in the stack has a latched lid; top of stack below clearance and retrieval height; labels visible; closet door still closes.
wrong: Puts a heavy bin on a light flimsy one (lid caves, contents crushed).
Stacks offset/mismatched footprints so the column leans and topples.
Stacks bins without lids so upper bins sit on contents.
fidelity: G: stack stability, footprint overlap and height clearance
notes: Generic stacking primitive in storage context; complements 'Retrieve bins' (unstack/restack).

interpretation: Fetch the specific requested bin (identified by label) from a stack or high shelf, which may require unstacking the bins above it and restacking them, then deliver it to the requester.
success: The requested bin is at the requester's location (or handed over); other bins are restacked stably in their original order; no bin dropped; nothing left strewn on the floor.
wrong: Pulls the bottom bin out from under the stack so the column falls.
Brings a similar-looking bin with the wrong label ('Xmas lights' vs 'Xmas ornaments').
Leaves the unstacked bins spread across the floor.
fidelity: G: unstack/restack reach and stability
user_sim: Hidden: which bin when the request is vague ('the camping stuff' when two bins qualify). Necessary question only when >1 label matches; unnecessary when a single label matches.
notes: Counterpart of 'Stack bins'; same retrieval skill used for luggage and holiday bins.

interpretation: Carry bins from one storage area to another (e.g. hall closet to basement) with two hands, lids on and upright, through doorways and possibly stairs, placing them at the destination in a stable arrangement.
success: All designated bins are at the destination, upright, lids on, contents intact (no tumble events), stacked stably; no wall/door scuffs along the route; source area left clear.
wrong: Drags a heavy bin down the stairs bumping each step.
Carries an open bin tilted so contents spill.
Leaves bins blocking the stairway or hallway mid-move.
fidelity: G: carried-load clearance through doorways and on stairs
notes: Carry skill shared with laundry baskets and moving boxes.

interpretation: Pack prepared donation items into bags/boxes by type (clothing separate from housewares), wrap breakables, close and label them 'DONATION', and stage them at the pickup spot clearly separated from trash bags.
success: All donation items are bagged/boxed, closed, labeled, at the staging area; no non-donation item inside; donation bags are visually distinct from and not adjacent to trash bags; breakables wrapped.
wrong: Uses black trash bags and stages them beside the garbage (gets thrown out).
Packs glassware unwrapped under heavy books.
