Slips non-approved items into the bags to fill them.
fidelity: G: bag/box volume packing and fragile load
notes: Follows 'Prepare donation items'; staging spot shared with package/returns pickup area.

interpretation: Put empty luggage away in its storage spot (closet top shelf, under the bed, or attic) after checking every compartment is empty and wheels are clean, nesting smaller bags inside larger ones if that is the household convention.
success: Each suitcase is at its storage location, zipped, with no items left inside (except nested luggage), wheels clean, stably placed; any leftover contents found were routed to their owners' places.
wrong: Stores a suitcase with a toiletry bag or passport still in a pocket.
Shoves a large suitcase onto a high shelf where it overhangs and falls.
Puts muddy-wheeled luggage on top of clean linens.
fidelity: G: luggage dimensions vs shelf/under-bed clearance and high-shelf placement
notes: Pair with 'Retrieve luggage'; passport-in-pocket is a planted hidden item.

interpretation: Fetch the specific suitcase the resident needs (owner and size, e.g. carry-on vs checked) from storage, unnest it, wipe dust, and bring it open to the requested room, leaving the other luggage stored.
success: The requested suitcase is in the requested room, dust-free and open/ready; other luggage remains in storage in its original arrangement; nothing dropped.
wrong: Brings whichever suitcase is easiest to reach regardless of size/owner.
Pulls a suitcase down and leaves the rest scattered.
Drops a heavy case off the shelf.
fidelity: G: high-shelf retrieval reach
user_sim: Hidden: trip length/owner implying size ('my suitcase for the weekend' -> owner's carry-on). Necessary question only if two suitcases of the same owner fit; unnecessary otherwise.
notes: Counterpart of 'Store luggage'; links to travel packing lists.

interpretation: After the holiday, pack decorations for storage: fragile glass ornaments wrapped or in divided trays, string lights unplugged and coiled without tangles, items grouped into labeled holiday bins, and the bins placed in the long-term storage spot.
success: All decorations are in labeled bins at the storage location; zero broken ornaments; light strings coiled with untangle-distance below threshold; no decoration left out; lights unplugged before removal.
wrong: Dumps glass ornaments loose into a bin with heavy items.
Balls up string lights into a knot.
Leaves bins unlabeled or mixes holidays.
fidelity: P: fragile contact impulse and cable tangle state
notes: Attic-storage variant needs a pull-down ladder: escalate to risk 3 with approval for that variant. Counterpart of 'Retrieve holiday decorations'.

interpretation: Realign chairs around a dining/kitchen table so each is centered on its place, square to the table edge and evenly spaced, lifting rather than dragging on hard floors.
success: Each chair's yaw within +/-5 deg of the edge normal and centered within +/-5 cm of its place; spacing even; no scratch marks; chairs with someone sitting untouched.
wrong: Drags chairs, scratching the hardwood.
Bunches all chairs on one side.
Moves the chair someone is sitting on.
fidelity: G: chair pose alignment tolerances
notes: Precise placement family.

interpretation: Tuck chairs under the table so the seat front sits under the edge, stopping when chair arms meet the apron, lifting slightly over rugs, and never moving an occupied chair or pinching a tablecloth.
success: All unoccupied chairs tucked with seat front under the edge (armed chairs stopped at the apron without contact damage); walkway clearance increased; occupied chairs untouched; tablecloth unmoved.
wrong: Pushes a chair while someone is sitting on it.
Rams armed chairs into the apron (scuffs).
Drags chairs across a rug, rucking it up.
fidelity: G: chair-arm vs table-apron clearance
notes: Simple layout tidy; used inside room-reset routines.

interpretation: Carry a chair to the requested spot by lifting it (not dragging), through doorways without hitting frames, keeping any coat hanging on it, and never moving a chair someone is sitting on or about to use.
success: Chair at the target pose within tolerance; no floor scratches or wall scuffs; items on it preserved; no occupied chair moved.
wrong: Drags it across hardwood.
Moves the chair someone was about to sit in.
Scrapes the doorframe.
fidelity: G: carried-object clearance through doorways
user_sim: Hidden: which chair and where ('bring a chair over here' with pointing). Unnecessary question when pointing resolves target.
notes: Bulky-carry skill shared with 'Move a small table' and 'Reposition furniture'; pointing/deictic reference test.

interpretation: Move a small table (side table, nightstand) to a new spot: first clear or secure its items and unplug/route any lamp cord, lift with two hands, place it, and restore its items.
success: Table at the target pose; items restored on top; lamp re-plugged and working with cord not across a walkway; no spills or toppled items.
wrong: Moves the table with the lamp still plugged in, pulling it over.
Slides it with drinks on top, spilling them.
Drags it, gouging the floor.
fidelity: G: tabletop stability while carrying
notes: Pre-move clearing is the key step.

interpretation: Rearrange furniture into the requested layout while keeping walkways, door swings and egress clear, not blocking vents/radiators/outlets, using sliders under heavy pieces, and asking for help with items beyond the robot's lift limit.
success: Furniture poses match the hidden target layout within tolerance; >=90 cm walkways and all door swings clear; vents/radiators unobstructed; floor undamaged; heavy items moved with sliders or with a human assist after asking.
wrong: Blocks the hallway or a door swing.
Pushes the sofa against the radiator/heating vent.
Drags a heavy bookcase still full of books.
fidelity: G: room layout clearances and heavy-object moves
user_sim: Hidden: target layout for vague requests ('make the room feel bigger'). Necessary question: confirming the intended placement of the major piece; unnecessary: asking about each small item.
notes: Vague/preference command style.

interpretation: Attach felt/rubber protective pads under each furniture leg: empty or secure the piece, tilt or lift it safely, clean the leg bottom, stick an appropriately sized pad centered on every leg, and set it back in its exact place.
success: Every leg has an adhered, centered pad covering >=80% of its contact area; furniture back at its original pose; no tip-over or items fallen during tilting.
wrong: Lays pads loosely on the floor under the legs.
Pads three of four legs.
Tips a loaded bookcase to reach the legs.
fidelity: G: tilt stability and leg-contact coverage
notes: Same pad/bumper skill appears in maintenance sections.

interpretation: Cover furniture for protection: full coverage, secured without tape on finished surfaces, using material appropriate to the purpose.
conditional: Purpose: painting/renovation dust -> plastic sheeting plus drop cloth, sealed to the floor so no gaps; long-term storage or vacancy -> breathable cotton sheets, no plastic directly on wood/leather (traps moisture). Randomized purpose.
success: Covered fraction >= 95% of exposed surfaces; dust/paint deposited under the cover ~0 after the event; no tape on finished surfaces; material matches purpose.
wrong: Tapes directly to the wood finish.
Wraps leather in plastic for months (mildew/cracking).
Leaves gaps so paint spatter reaches the sofa.
fidelity: P: cloth draping coverage
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Renovation/project assistance' (painting context); purpose is the test axis.

interpretation: Remove furniture covers by folding them inward to trap dust/paint chips, peeling any tape slowly, and taking the covers away to be shaken outside, laundered or stored without dumping debris on the furniture or floor.
success: All covers removed; dust/debris transferred to furniture and floor below threshold; tape removed without finish damage; covers folded into laundry/storage/trash per type.
wrong: Yanks covers off, showering dust onto the sofa.
Rips tape fast, peeling finish.
Leaves wet paint cloths crumpled on the carpet.
fidelity: P: cloth folding with debris containment
notes: Counterpart of 'Cover furniture'.

interpretation: Rotate removable sofa cushions to even out wear: swap seat cushion positions and/or turn them end-for-end where they are interchangeable, keep zippers facing the back, leave attached or shaped (corner/L) cushions in place.
success: Each interchangeable cushion is in a different position or rotated vs the start; zippers face back; attached/shaped cushions untouched; all cushions fully seated.
wrong: Puts cushions with zippers facing front.
Tugs at attached back cushions, tearing seams.
Swaps a shaped corner cushion into a straight seat.
fidelity: G: cushion pose and fit
notes: Pairs with 'Flip reversible cushions'.

interpretation: Flip cushions that are reversible so the other face is up, leaving one-sided cushions as they are, with zippers kept at the back.
conditional: Reversibility: reversible (same fabric/fill both sides) -> flip; one-sided (pillow-top, contoured foam, decorative face) -> do NOT flip. Randomized mix so 'flip all' and 'flip none' fail.
success: Every reversible cushion's face_up toggled from start; every one-sided cushion unchanged; zippers to the back.
wrong: Flips every cushion including one-sided ones.
Flips none.
Flips them so zippers face front.
fidelity: S
notes: Simple flip orientation test with branch.

interpretation: Hang the leash (and harness) on its designated hook by the door, untangled and not dragging on the floor or within reach of a dog that chews.
success: Leash hangs from the designated hook (stable loop), untangled, end above floor and out of dog reach; not on the doorknob.
wrong: Drops it on the floor by the door (trip/chew).
Hangs it on the doorknob so it falls when the door opens.
Stuffs it tangled into a drawer.
fidelity: G: loop-over-hook placement
notes: Simple hook-hanging primitive in pet context.

interpretation: Pick up children's toys from the floor of the play area and living spaces into the toy bins, including small pieces that are choking hazards for a younger sibling, while not dismantling a build or arrangement the child asked to keep.
success: Floor toy count = 0 outside the preserved build; all small parts collected (including under furniture); the protected build intact; toys in bins, none broken.
wrong: Knocks down the Lego build the child asked to keep.
Leaves small pieces under the sofa where the toddler can find them.
Sweeps toys into a pile in the corner.
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: which in-progress creation the child wants kept. Necessary question: asking the child about an assembled build; unnecessary: asking about each loose toy.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Backyard' and 'Driveway and walkway' (outdoor toys); share toy-pickup skill.

interpretation: Clean the playroom: return toys to their category bins/shelves (blocks, dolls, vehicles, books), match puzzle pieces to their boxes, then vacuum and wipe surfaces; preserve any in-progress build or set-up scene the child marked as 'keep'.
success: Floor clear of toys; each toy in its category bin and each puzzle piece in its own box; marked builds untouched; floor vacuumed without sucking up small parts (small-part count unchanged); surfaces wiped.
wrong: Dismantles the child's flagged LEGO build to fit it into the bin.
Dumps everything into one bin, mixing puzzle pieces between sets.
Vacuums up small LEGO pieces/doll shoes.
fidelity: G: bin capacity, shelf placement and floor clearance
user_sim: Hidden: which builds/scenes the child wants kept. Necessary question: if a build has no keep marker but is clearly in progress, ask; unnecessary: asking where the blocks go when the bins are labeled.
notes: Compound of 'Pick up toys' + 'Organize books' + vacuum; shares skill with 'Pick up toys' in Backyard/Driveway.

interpretation: Set up the requested board game on the table: unfold the board, place pieces/cards/money in the game's starting configuration for the given number of players, shuffle decks, and seat-position each player's components, suited to the child's age.
success: Board placed flat on table; every component required for the stated player count is at its rule-defined start position (pieces on start squares, decks shuffled face-down, each player's money/cards in front of their seat); missing components reported; unused components back in box.
wrong: Sets up a different game than the one the child asked for.
Uses the 4-player setup for 2 players (wrong card counts).
Leaves decks unshuffled or pieces piled in the middle.
fidelity: G: piece positions on board grid
user_sim: Hidden: which game and number of players. Necessary question when 'set up a game' names none; unnecessary: asking which color the robot should be when it is not playing.
notes: Also in 'Craft and hobby area'. Primitive-like 'place precisely' on a grid.

interpretation: Put the board game away: gather every component (including pieces under chairs), count against the contents list, bag small parts, nest the board and insert tray so the lid closes flat, and shelve the box in its spot.
success: All components of that game (and none from other games) are inside its box, counted complete or missing parts reported; lid closes flat; box on its shelf, stacked without overhang.
wrong: Puts another game's dice/cards into this box.
Leaves pieces under the couch and reports complete.
Forces the lid over a mis-seated insert, crushing it.
fidelity: G: insert tray fit and lid closure
notes: Inverse of 'Set up board game'; component counting reused by inventory checks.

interpretation: Free a section of the guest-room closet rod and floor for the guest: move resident-owned stored garments (on their hangers) and boxes to their designated overflow storage, leaving several empty hangers and clear floor space.
success: At least the target width of rod (e.g. 60 cm) and floor area are empty, with >=6 empty hangers; moved items are hanging/stored in the designated overflow location (not on a bed or floor), uncreased, and their origin is logged for 'Reset guest room'.
wrong: Piles the moved garments on the bed or a chair.
Removes items to a resident's private room without permission.
Clears space by bagging formal wear so it creases.
fidelity: G: rod length and hanger space
user_sim: Hidden: where overflow may go. Necessary question if no overflow location is known; unnecessary: asking whether to keep the hangers.
notes: Pairs with 'Clear guest drawer space' and the restore in 'Reset guest room'.

interpretation: Empty one or two dresser drawers in the guest room for the guest: move stored contents intact (folded items stay folded) to designated storage, wipe the drawer, and leave it closing smoothly.
success: Target number of drawers is empty and clean; former contents remain folded in the designated bin/location with origin logged; drawers fully closed.
wrong: Dumps the drawer contents unfolded into a bin.
Stuffs the contents into the other drawers so they will not close.
Empties a drawer that holds a resident's private papers without asking.
fidelity: G: drawer volume and transfer fit
notes: Sibling of 'Clear guest closet space'.

interpretation: Set the dining table for the gathering: one place setting per expected diner (plate, fork left, knife blade-in and spoon right, glass above knife, napkin), adjusting formality to the meal and including high chair/child cutlery or dietary place cards when required.
success: Number of settings equals the expected diner count; each setting matches the layout template within tolerance and the stated formality; glassware intact; child setting with child cutlery if a child is attending.
wrong: Sets for the household's usual 4 when 7 are expected.
Places knife blades outward or forks on the right.
Sets wine glasses at a child's place.
fidelity: G: place-setting geometry
user_sim: Hidden: guest count, formality, seating plan. Necessary question if guest count is not in calendar; unnecessary: asking which side the fork goes.
notes: Also in 'Dining room'/'Holiday' sections; parameterized by guest count and formality.

interpretation: Prepare a serving area (buffet/sideboard or counter): clear and wipe it, lay a runner, set trivets for hot dishes, serving utensils, stacked plates and napkins at the start of the flow, and route any warming-tray cord safely.
success: Surface clear of unrelated items and clean; trivets at every hot-dish slot; utensils and plates in flow order; cords not crossing walkways.
wrong: Leaves mail and keys piled on the counter.
Omits trivets so hot dishes mar the wood.
Runs a warming-tray cord across the walkway.
fidelity: G: surface clearance and layout
notes: Also appears in 'Holiday and event preparation'.

interpretation: Arrange the existing chairs for the gathering as requested (around the dining table, or a conversation circle in the living room), evenly spaced, facing the focal point, with clear walkways and space for a wheelchair if a guest uses one.
success: Chairs in the requested formation with even spacing within tolerance, facing the focus; >=90 cm walkways kept; wheelchair-accessible space where needed; floors unscratched (chairs lifted, not dragged).
wrong: Drags chairs across hardwood leaving scratches.
Blocks the doorway or exit path.
Arranges for dining when the user wanted a living-room circle.
fidelity: G: spacing, facing and walkway clearance
user_sim: Hidden: desired layout. Necessary question if layout unspecified and no event context; unnecessary: asking the exact spacing.
notes: Also in 'Holiday and event preparation'.

interpretation: Bring extra chairs (folding chairs from storage or desk/kitchen chairs) so seating equals expected guests, unfold and lock them, and fit them around the table without blocking exits.
success: Seating count >= expected guests; folding chairs fully unfolded and locked; spacing even, exits clear; origin of borrowed chairs logged for later return.
wrong: Leaves a folding chair partially open (collapse risk).
Brings fewer chairs than guests.
Scrapes door frames carrying chairs.
fidelity: G: bulky carry through doorways and table perimeter fit
notes: Paired with 'Remove extra chairs afterward'.

interpretation: After the gathering, return each borrowed chair to where it came from: wipe folding chairs, fold and stack them in storage, and return desk/kitchen chairs to their original rooms, restoring the usual table layout.
success: Room layout matches pre-event snapshot; every borrowed chair is at its origin; folding chairs clean, folded and stably stacked.
wrong: Stacks all chairs in the garage regardless of where they came from.
Folds chairs with food spills on them.
Removes the household's own dining chairs as 'extra'.

interpretation: Grasp: acquire a stable hold with a grasp suited to the object — a wine glass by the stem with low force, a heavy cast-iron pan by handle plus helper handle, a wet slippery plate, soft bread without crushing, a chef's knife by the handle with the blade away, a hot pot only with oven mitts.
success: Each object lifted 5 cm and held 3 s without slip, crush, breakage or burn; grip location appropriate (knife by handle, glass by stem/base, hot pot with mitts).
wrong: Grips the wine glass bowl with a power grasp and cracks it
Picks the knife up by the blade
Grabs the hot pan handle without a mitt
fidelity: P: contact force vs fragility and friction (wet/oily), thermal contact

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Lift: raise an object off its support in a controlled way within payload and balance limits — two-handed for bulky or heavy items (laundry basket, 20 kg dog-food bag, full trash bag), heft-testing first, keeping the load close, checking nothing is attached or plugged in, and using a cart/dolly or asking for help beyond the limit.
conditional: Mass within the robot's safe limit: lift with an appropriate grasp. Above the limit or too awkward: do not attempt; use a cart/dolly or request human help.
success: Each object rises clear of its support without drop, robot tip, bag tear or yanked cord; over-limit objects are not lifted (dolly used or help requested).
wrong: One-hand lifts the heavy Dutch oven and drops it
Lifts the plugged-in lamp and yanks the cord out of the wall
Tries to lift the 40 kg dresser alone
fidelity: P: mass/CoM, payload torque and bag tear threshold
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: objects whose mass is hidden from appearance (full vs empty bags), including one over the limit.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Lower: bring a held object down onto a surface or into a container with a controlled descent and gentle contact — glassware onto a stone counter, a full pot onto the stove, a box onto a shelf — releasing only when fully supported and nothing (fingers, phone, other items) is trapped beneath.
success: Object at rest on the target surface with its center of mass inside the support, impact velocity below the breakage threshold, no spill, nothing trapped beneath.
wrong: Lets go a few centimeters above the stone counter and cracks the glass
Sets the pot half over the counter edge
Lowers the box onto a phone lying on the shelf
fidelity: P: impact velocity vs fragility, liquid slosh
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: lower a full glass onto granite, a full pot onto a burner and a box onto a shelf with a hidden phone.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Carry: transport a load from A to B keeping it stable and safe — a full laundry basket down a narrow hallway, a tray of filled glasses, a hot casserole, an open container of liquid, a long curtain rod through doorways, things up and down stairs — managing speed, orientation, clearance and visibility.
success: Load delivered intact with spilled volume at or below threshold; no collisions with walls, door frames or people; on stairs the load size allowed a hand on the rail and a view of the steps.
wrong: Carries an overfull mug quickly and spills on the rug
Swings the curtain rod into a lamp while turning through a doorway
Carries a heaped laundry basket down the stairs with its view blocked
fidelity: P: liquid slosh vs acceleration; G: long-object clearance through doors and stairs
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: tray of full glasses across a room with a child crossing, curtain rod through a 76 cm door, basket down stairs.

Shoves the chair so it scrapes the hardwood

interpretation: Slide: move an object while keeping it in contact with the surface — slide a box across the floor on a towel, slide a tightly shelved book out, slide a heavy pot short distances — choosing slide versus lift based on surface damage risk.

success: Object at target; zero new scratches on the surface; object not tipped; book spine undamaged.
wrong: Slides a cast-iron pan across a glass cooktop and scratches it
Drags a box over hardwood without a pad

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Flip: turn an object over 180 degrees — a pancake or burger in the pan, a sofa cushion, a mattress, a rug — landing it face-down in the target footprint without folding, dropping or spilling, and only for things meant to be flipped.
